parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or expression; hate-crime and hate-speech coverage since 2018/19; no documented border, document or police-profiling friction for trans visitors, and in a well-documented state that silence is moderately positive. The main traveller-facing exposure is the October 2025 company-wide swimming-pool chain rule barring trans customers from choosing changing rooms — a current, ordinary-facility access restriction, though limited in scope (one chain, not a national statute) and under legal contestation, with changing-room access elsewhere unsettled. Countervailing: functioning institutions, hate-crime recording, and a 2019 travel-index ranking. Organised political opposition, contested hate-speech enforcement and intimidation of advocates weigh, but largely describe the domestic activist sphere rather than visitor exposure. Clinical/legal-recognition restrictions are resident-facing climate signals only. Below the acceptance-with-working-remedy tier, above the widespread-service-denial tier.
